articles.title: Post your questions for Alex Cox
articles.summary: As the cult director of Repo Man and Sid and Nancy prepares to release his final film, Dead Souls, he takes your questions. Everybody has their swansong, whether they know it or not.
body: If it really is his last film, the fiercely independent British film-maker can look back on a helluva run. He broke through with 1984 punk classic Repo Man, then went on to direct Gary Oldman as Sid Vicious in Sid and Nancy. He made the political “western” Walker in 1987, starring Ed Harris – then from 1988 to 1994 introduced viewers to cult and overlooked films as the original presenter of BBC Two’s Moviedrome, essentially doing film nerd YouTube decades before YouTube existed.

He ended up making films in Mexico in the 1990s, including the brilliant Highway Patrolman, then returned to his home town of Liverpool for Three Businessmen and The Revengers Tragedy. Back in the US Cox made Searchers 2.0 (an update of the classic western), Repo Chick (a sequel) and sci-fi comedy Bill the Galactic Hero.

articles.title: ‘It’s the gay Titanic!’ Inside La Bola Negra, the maximalist queer spectacular bound for Oscars glory
articles.summary: Oozing panache and bagging awards already, La Bola Negra is an eye-popping war and prejudice epic starring Penélope Cruz in a blond wig and Glenn Close speaking Spanish. We meet the ex-lovers who dreamed it up.
body: When Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo – the directing duo known in their native Spain as “Los Javis” – began writing their queer epic La Bola Negra, they weren’t thinking about whether it would be stylish (which it is) or win numerous awards (which it has) or capture what they refer to as “the anti-fascist zeitgeist” (which it does). Instead, they thought only of scale. “I’m done with LGBTQ+ movies being niche,” says Ambrossi. “I was like, ‘Let’s make the biggest, gayest war movie ever.’” Job done.

Throw in spectacular set pieces, Ken Russell-style visual flair, cameos from a blond-wigged Penélope Cruz and a Spanish-speaking Glenn Close, and the result is a maximalist collage where the Spanish civil war sits side-by-side with Grindr hook-ups. “We loved imagining scenes that you don’t usually have in queer movies,” says Ambrossi, citing the spectacular opening sequence in which a Spanish village is bombed by Italian fascists. “A lot of people have said they’ve been missing something like this. They want to buy popcorn and be given a big movie like Titanic.” His eyes widen. “This is the gay Titanic!”

articles.title: Camila Mendes, Leslie Bibb Shooting ‘Upgraded 2’ in Venice, Where Biennale Art Show Is Part of Rom-Com’s Storyline
articles.summary: Shooting is underway in Venice on “Upgraded 2,” the sequel to Amazon MGM Studios’ buzzy 2024 rom-com “Upgraded” that, as announced, is set to star Leslie Bibb alongside Camila Mendes.
body: In the sequel to the modern-day “Cinderella” tale, on which cameras started rolling in Venice on Oct. 21, Ana is now seemingly seeking to make her mark at the Venice Biennale art exhibition, the world’s oldest contemporary art fair. Becca Gleason, who is helming the sequel — taking over from “Upgraded” director Carlson Young — has been shooting on the terrace of Ca’ Giustinian, the Biennale headquarters that overlook the lagoon’s Grand Canal; in the neo-Gothic Palazzo Franchetti near the Accademia bridge, which serves as a Biennale exhibition space; and at the luxurious Moro Venice restaurant. So far, there are no indications on what Bibb’s role is.
Luke Roberts and Justin Matthews, who penned the first film, also wrote the screenplay for the sequel.

articles.title: Japanese-Brazilian Grief Drama ‘Yellow Chrysanthemum,’ Set During the 2014 Soccer World Cup, Joins Tokyo Gap-Financing Market
articles.summary: A Japanese-Brazilian teenager forced to face a family loss nobody will talk about is at the heart of “Yellow Chrysanthemum,” the first feature from Japanese-Brazilian director André Hayato Saito, which is among the projects at this year’s Tokyo Gap-Financing Market.
body: That rejection stems from an old wound. When Erika was 7, her cousin Yam, who was also her closest friend, vanished during a traditional festival in the Liberdade neighborhood while Erika’s mother was looking after the children. The family has been locked in guilty silence ever since.

Erika’s friendship with Bianca, a Black classmate mourning the recent death of her mother, stirs up the feelings she has long pushed down. Bianca makes no secret of her grief, and as the two girls grow closer, Erika’s family can no longer avoid confronting Yam’s absence.

“I vividly remember being a little boy, sitting in the bathroom with my father, when I suddenly asked him where we go after we die. He paused for a moment and answered with a long and profound silence,” Saito said.

Growing up in a Japanese-Brazilian household, Saito came to see how silence in his family could express love and respect while also hiding pain. His short films have dealt with grief, memory, identity and life between two cultures, and he described the feature as a continuation of that work.

articles.title: Academy CEO Bill Kramer Maps Oscars’ Global Ambitions in Tokyo: ‘Parasite’ Win Was ‘a Pivot, a Shift’
articles.summary: The Academy plans to keep taking the Oscars global, from recruiting members in underrepresented countries to streaming the ceremony free on YouTube, its leadership said in Tokyo, where CEO Bill Kramer said the share of members living outside the U.S. has grown from around 5% to 25% in a decade.
body: Kramer described the membership shift as part of a push for a more diverse and inclusive Academy. A decade ago, he said, only 5% to 6% of members were based outside the U.S. “Now it’s 25%, and that number is growing.” The Academy has about 70 members in Japan.

“People are making movies around the world, people are watching films that are not in their native language more and more,” Kramer said. “We’re making movies everywhere, we’re viewing movies in a much more nimble and accessible way, and the Academy needs to reflect that.”

Kramer pointed out that every category at the most recent Oscars had international representation, including best picture. “Of course, everybody remembers the moment when ‘Parasite’ won. It was sort of a pivot, a shift, I think, in our thinking about what was possible with global cinema at the Oscars, and that continues,” he said, referring to Bong Joon Ho’s 2020 best picture winner.

articles.summary: Immersive portrait of mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson as they seek to become the first people to ski down Everest’s north face. With some of its showings in the huge Imax format, this National Geographic-backed documentary feels like a callback to the early, glory days of large-format…
body: The lurid palette of this kit does in fact become a bit distracting when we get back to the mountain climbing stuff, and if you want to just relax and look at the stunning landscape you need to train your eyes to ignore the fluorescent jackets obstructing the view. That’s not criticising the cinematography itself; it is pin-sharp thanks to the most advanced kinds of lenses and drone technology. But it’s safe to say the ethics aired here are a far murkier affair.

articles.title: Taiwan-Japan Film Fund Daily Capital Launches at Tokyo Market, Backs Period Romance ‘Love Ends in Bloom’
articles.summary: Daily Capital, a new fund focused on Taiwan-Japan film and television co-productions, launched on the Tokyo International Film Festival market TIFFCOM’s opening day at the “Taiwan Originals: Project Showcase” event.
body: The name “Daily” reflects the idea that meaningful progress is built through daily efforts, Chang said at the launch.

In Japan, Daily Capital has identified K2 Pictures and Remow as co-development partners. Founded by producer Kii Muneyuki, K2 Pictures brings together Japanese filmmakers including Iwai Shunji, Miike Takashi, Nishikawa Miwa and Kore-eda Hirokazu. Remow is backed by Japanese entertainment and media companies including Shueisha, Toei, Amuse, Shochiku, TBS Holdings and Fuji Media Holdings, with access to established IP libraries and distribution networks.

“Investment amounts will vary according to each project’s scale and needs, whether it’s a film, series or animation. We expect to come in during development or pre-production, contribute to script discussions and help assemble the core creative team. We also aim to keep the primary capital recovery period within three years,” Chang said.

The fund plans to pair Japan’s IP and production know-how with Taiwan’s flexible financing and co-production experience. It will also tap local production incentives and distribution networks to reach audiences beyond Japanese- and Mandarin-speaking markets.

articles.title: Peter Asher: Everywhere Man review – music-biz face from Beatles-buddy pop act to superstar producer
articles.summary: Backstory of modest industry veteran who started out as one half of pop duo Peter and Gordon, and went on to produce acts such as James Taylor and Linda Ronstadt. Rock’n’roll is notorious for its tales of bad behaviour: throwing TVs out of the window, mountains of cocaine, parades of groupies … but…
body: At one point Asher says he wasn’t much of a pop star, and subsequent events suggest he was probably right. He appears to have been more comfortable away from the spotlight, thereby allowing him to become a ubiquitous figure in the Beatles’ orbit in swinging 60s London to which the title alludes. He was a co-owner of supercool art gallery Indica (where Lennon first met Yoko Ono), though given it only lasted two years, possibly he wasn’t all that great at that, either. It was the Beatles’ connection, though, that allowed him to really come into his own, when he was appointed head of A&R at the newly formed Apple Records, with his own top floor office in the Savile Row building.

Throughout this parade of achievement, Asher cuts an impressively self-possessed figure, unassuming in many ways but also not hiding his light under a bushel. The appreciation he gets from his big-name collaborators is clear enough, but he also gives houseroom to somewhat more tangential figures, with Carole King in particular coming across strongly. But it’s the interactions with late former partner Waller that are probably the most resonant, with the virtual duet Asher sets up being especially moving.

articles.title: Star Trek actor Walter Koenig, who played Pavel Chekov, dies aged 90
articles.summary: He played the eager Russian crewman in the original Star Trek series and later appeared in Babylon 5.
body: Walter Koenig, who played the spirited Russian crewman Pavel Chekov in the original Star Trek TV series, has died aged 90.

The US actor was a mainstay on the show as the eager and earnest navigator of the Starship Enterprise, from season two in 1967 until it ended in 1969, later reprising his role in the six original cast movies from 1979 through to 1991.
In the mid-late 1990s, Koenig portrayed a very different character, the ruthless Psi Corps telepath Alfred Bester, in another sci-fi space series, Babylon 5.
His Star Trek co-star George Takei led the tributes, external on social media on Monday, writing: "Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend."

articles.title: 6 Music Festival 2027 heads to Newcastle
articles.summary: The station's flagship festival will return to Tyneside after 12 years.
body: BBC Radio 6 Music has announced the 2027 edition of its annual festival will take place in Newcastle.
After four years in Greater Manchester, the festival will take place across Newcastle's independent and grassroots venues in March with five days of performances and DJ sets.
Tyneside last hosted the festival in 2015 but principal advisor for events and culture at Newcastle City Council, Jim Mawdsley, said since then "Newcastle has become a true music city".
Head of BBC Radio 6 Music Samantha Moy said: "The city and the region have such a rich musical legacy and a thriving creative community, which will make for another wonderful setting."

articles.title: Academy CEO Bill Kramer Makes the Case for a More Global Oscars at Tokyo Film Festival
articles.summary: Kramer says international membership growth, the Oscars-YouTube deal, and a new festival-qualifying pathway to nomination are all part of the organization’s expanding worldwide ambitions.
body: The U.S. may be growing ever more isolationist under the “America First” rubric of President Donald Trump, but the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences remains steadfastly global in its outlook and ambitions.

That was the thrust of Academy CEO Bill Kramer ’s comments at the Tokyo International Film Festival on Wednesday, where he spoke at length about his organization’s ongoing efforts to bring more international filmmakers and film lovers into the Oscars fold.
“This is all part of our drive to create a more diverse and inclusive academy,” he said.
Kramer also underscored that Oscars nominations have already begun to reflect the increasingly cosmopolitan tastes of the member base.
